brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack hangs on a wall
requirements.evidence: Three stacked bases (piece:0,0,0/1/2), with slot 0 on every level as the back face. That face has keyhole hangers on levels 0 and 2 and nothing on level 1, so it sits flat against the wall.
accessory:0#0,0#0 and accessory:2#0,0#0 (hex-acc-keyhole), on the bottom and top levels for two wall screws.
9 hex-acc-hook plates (18 hooks) in slots 2, 3 and 4 on every level. A cable coil and two rolls of gaffer tape hang on them to show it in use.

requirements.requirement: Holds the weight of tools on the wall (load)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only and knows nothing about strength or load ratings. How much it holds depends on the print material and the wall screws.

finish.summary: I built a wall tool rack: one column of three bases stacked on cell 0,0. Two keyhole hangers sit on the back face, at the bottom and top levels. Nine hook plates cover the front and the two front side faces on all three levels. Each plate has two hooks, so that's 18 hooks. The joints are bolted. The cap rule added one solid cap, and the check still lists 6 side faces that could take a cap; that's a note, not an error. The rule check passed and the mesh-collision check came back clear. For show, I hung a coiled cable and two rolls of gaffer tape on hooks. The configurator wouldn't hang a prop on the lowest front hook because the model sits on the bench, so the prop would have gone through it. On the wall that hook would be clear. The configurator only checks that parts fit, so nothing here shows how much weight the rack can hold.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
